title: Campania Goes From Metano's Premium Region to Its Discount One
dek: A look at today's fuel prices in Campania, and the four-month weekly trend showing LPG and natural gas moving in opposite directions relative to the rest of Italy.
executive_summary: On November 22, 2026 (the most recent completed day), self-service Benzina in Campania averaged €1.9509/L, down 0.30% from two days earlier and essentially in line with Italy's €1.9565/L average. Gasolio slipped to €2.2212/L (-0.20%), also just under the €2.2267/L national mark. GPL ticked up to €0.8203/L (+0.34%), still running about 1.5% cheaper than the €0.8329/L national average. Metano held flat at €1.9554/L, a full 7.1% below Italy's €2.1054/L average -- the widest regional discount of the four fuels today. Across 2,122 registered stations, 1,845 (87.0%) reported a price today.

Zoom out to the 16 weeks of data tracked since July 21, 2026, though, and the real story is how much Campania's relative position has shifted -- in opposite directions for GPL and Metano. Campania's GPL started the summer running about 5.4% below the national average and has since closed most of that gap, now sitting only 1.5-1.6% under Italy; its Metano did the reverse, starting essentially at parity (even a touch above) the national price in July and ending up roughly 7% cheaper by November, the sharpest divergence of any fuel tracked for this region. Benzina and Gasolio, meanwhile, have largely tracked the national curve point-for-point, rising into a mid-September peak and easing back since.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina: Tracking the National Curve, Almost Tick for Tick
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Campania closed November 22 at €1.9509 per liter, down €0.0059 (-0.30%) from the November 20 reading and a touch below Italy's national average of €1.9565/L. Served-pump prices followed the same pattern, at €2.0458/L regionally versus €2.0983/L nationally.

Across the 16 tracked weeks, Campania's Benzina has moved almost in lockstep with the rest of the country: both climbed from the €1.97-1.98/L range in late July to a shared peak in the week of September 21 (Campania €2.1650/L, Italy €2.1669/L), then eased back by an almost identical -9.4% into the week of November 16 (Campania €1.9617/L, Italy €1.9635/L). The two series have stayed within a few tenths of a cent of each other for four months -- Benzina is the one fuel where this region's prices are basically a mirror of the national trend.

fuel_sections.heading: Gasolio: A Steeper Summer Climb, A Slightly Gentler Comedown
paragraphs: Diesel in Campania eased to €2.2212/L self-service on November 22, down €0.0045 (-0.20%) day-over-day and just under Italy's €2.2267/L average. At the pump with service, the region averaged €2.3271/L against a €2.3789/L national figure.

Over the full tracked window, Campania's Gasolio rose 2.4% from the week of July 20 (€2.1774/L) to the week of November 16 (€2.2295/L), slightly less than Italy's 2.6% increase (€2.1747/L to €2.2312/L) over the same span. Both series peaked in the week of September 21 -- Campania at €2.3638/L, Italy at €2.3736/L -- and have since retreated, with Campania's pullback (-5.7%) a shade smaller than the national one (-6.0%). The net effect: Campania's diesel discount to the national average has stayed roughly constant all autumn, around half a cent to a cent per liter.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL: The Region That's Catching Up to the National Price
paragraphs: GPL nudged up to €0.8203/L in Campania on November 22, a 0.34% day-over-day rise, and remains the one fuel where the region still undercuts the national average by a clear margin -- €0.8329/L nationally, a gap of about 1.5%.

That gap used to be much wider. In the week of July 20, Campania's GPL averaged €0.7179/L against a national €0.7592/L -- a 5.4% discount. By the week of November 16, Campania had risen to €0.8168/L against Italy's €0.8302/L, a gap of just 1.6%. In percentage terms, Campania's GPL climbed 13.8% over the 16 tracked weeks versus 9.4% nationally -- the region's LPG prices are rising faster than the rest of the country and steadily closing the gap, even though Campania remains the cheaper option for now.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano: From a Small Premium to Campania's Biggest Discount
paragraphs: Metano was unchanged at €1.9554/L in Campania on November 22 -- the only fuel with zero day-over-day movement -- and that flat price already sits 7.1% below Italy's €2.1054/L national average, the widest gap of any of the four fuels tracked today.

This is the most dramatic trend shift in the region's data. In the week of July 20, Campania's Metano (€1.5129/L) was actually slightly above the national average (€1.4999/L) -- a small premium of about 0.9%. Nationally, Metano then climbed hard through the autumn gas-price run-up, rising 40.8% by the week of November 16 to €2.1114/L; Campania rose too, but by a smaller 29.3%, to €1.9554/L. That gap in growth rates flipped the region's position entirely -- from a price slightly above the national average in July to one running about 7% below it now -- by far the largest swing, in either direction, of any fuel in this region's four-month tracked history.

network_section.heading: Network Coverage: 1,845 of 2,122 Stations Reporting
paragraphs: Campania's registry listed 2,122 stations as of today, with 1,845 (87.0%) submitting a price. That reporting rate is slightly below Italy's national average of 90.4% (21,679 of 23,977 stations), putting Campania in the lower-middle of the pack for data completeness.

The registered count has crept up steadily since tracking began -- from 2,117 stations in the week of July 20 to 2,122 today -- a net gain of 5 stations, mostly new registrations rather than closures. The reporting rate has held fairly steady around 86-87% for most of the period, which means the regional averages above are built on a consistent, representative slice of the network rather than a shifting subset, giving the week-over-week comparisons more weight.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made
paragraphs: Every part of this report -- pulling the day's price data, picking which of Italy's 20 regions to spotlight, computing the weekly trend comparisons, and writing the analysis above -- runs automatically each morning through an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. The region rotation is deterministic and date-based (an alphabetical cycle through all 20 regions, self-correcting if a day is missed), not a human choosing what looks interesting; the prose is generated fresh from that day's actual numbers rather than reused or lightly edited from a prior report.

That's a different model from the spreadsheet most people reach for first: a manually-maintained Excel file needs someone to re-download the source data, re-paste it, recheck the formulas, and rewrite the commentary every single day -- and it usually doesn't happen on weekends or busy mornings. This pipeline runs daily regardless, publishes straight to a live dashboard, and produces a written report alongside it, which is the argument for building this kind of thing with AI tooling instead of maintaining it by hand.

pull_quote: Campania's Metano started July priced slightly above the rest of Italy -- it now sits 7% below the national average, the biggest swing of any fuel tracked in the region's four-month history.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Campania. The region's self-service Metano price has quietly flipped from a small premium over the Italian average in July to running about 7% cheaper than the rest of the country today -- the sharpest shift in Campania's four months of tracked data. GPL tells a related story in reverse: Campania's LPG used to run 5.4% below the national average and has since closed most of that gap to just 1.5%, rising faster than Italy as a whole.

Today's self-service prices in Campania: Benzina €1.9509/L, Gasolio €2.2212/L, GPL €0.8203/L, Metano €1.9554/L -- compared against national averages of €1.9565, €2.2267, €0.8329 and €2.1054 respectively, across 1,845 of 2,122 registered stations reporting.

This report -- the data pull, the region rotation, the week-over-week trend analysis, and the writing itself -- is generated automatically every single day by an unattended pipeline I built with Claude Code. No spreadsheet, no manual re-download, no copy-pasting formulas each morning: just a dashboard and a report that update themselves. It's a small example of what's possible when you let AI tools own a repetitive daily workflow instead of a human doing it by hand.
